title: Lanczos approximation of matrix functions: worst-case approximation factor
summary: Compare the $t$-step Lanczos function approximation $y_t=V_t h(T_t)V_t^*b$ with the best approximation in $\mathcal{K}_t(A,b)$, under $T_t=V_t^*AV_t$.

task.description_zh: Compare the $t$-step Lanczos function approximation $y_t=V_t h(T_t)V_t^*b$ with the best approximation in $\mathcal K_t(A,b)$. Assume $T_t=V_t^*AV_t$.
description_paragraphs: Compare the $t$-step Lanczos function approximation $y_t=V_t h(T_t)V_t^*b$ with the best approximation in $\mathcal{K}_t(A,b)$, under $T_t=V_t^*AV_t$.

model.instance: The unknown matrix $A\in\mathbb C^{d\times d}$ is Hermitian positive definite, satisfies $\kappa(A)=\kappa>1$, and has at least $t+1$ distinct eigenvalues. The vector $b\ne0,\alpha\in\mathbb R$ and function $h$ are public; either $h$ or $h(z)/z$ belongs to the specified Stieltjes class.

operations.query_signature: Input any vector v in C^d
operations.order_convention: Native linear action of the specified matrix; no derivative order of an unregistered scalar function is implied.

feedback_quality.description: Exact complex vector responses, without observation noise or rounding

operations.coupling: One fixed Hermitian matrix; queries are determined by the exact Lanczos recurrence starting from b
operations.index_control: The algorithm selects vectors and an available channel; block width is charged by column.

oracle.query_domain_description: Right products map C^d to C^d, with only the stated channel available. A q-column block costs q queries. Entries, inverse actions, shifted solves, and matrix-function actions are not additional free feedback.
oracle.description_zh: The data $d,t,\kappa,\alpha,h,b$ are public and $A$ is hidden. For any complex vector $v$, the interface returns exact $Av$. Internal complex arithmetic and scalar function evaluations are free.
description_paragraphs: The data $d,t,\kappa,\alpha,h,b$ are public and $A$ is hidden. For any complex vector $v$, the interface returns exact $Av$. Internal complex arithmetic and scalar function evaluations are free.

output.allowed_postprocessing: The output must be the fixed Lanczos-FA value. A different algorithm or Krylov approximation cannot be substituted.
output.certificate_requirement: Only the true-loss guarantee is required; no computable certificate is requested.
output.description_zh: Return the fixed algorithm's $y_t$. Substituting the best Krylov approximation would change the object being evaluated.
description_paragraphs: Return the fixed algorithm's $y_t$. Substituting the best Krylov approximation would change the object being evaluated.

metric.normalization: Use the source ratio conventions $0/0=1$ and $1/0=+\infty$. The quantity is an approximation factor, not exact-zero query complexity.
metric.finiteness_conditions: The specified dimension is finite, and the model and spectral assumptions hold.
metric.description_zh: Define $\|z\|_{A^\alpha}=(z^*A^\alpha z)^{1/2}$ and $\mathcal K_t(A,b)=\operatorname{span}\{b,Ab,\ldots,A^{t-1}b\}$. The approximation factor is $\mathcal C=\|h(A)b-y_t\|_{A^\alpha}/\min_{y\in\mathcal K_t(A,b)}\|h(A)b-y\|_{A^\alpha}$, with conventions $0/0=1$ and positive numbers divided by zero equal $+\infty$.
description_paragraphs:
Define the weighted norm $\|z\|_{A^\alpha}=(z^*A^\alpha z)^{1/2}$ and Krylov space $\mathcal{K}_t(A,b)=\operatorname{span}\{b,Ab,\ldots,A^{t-1}b\}$. Compare the fixed Lanczos output with the best approximation in that space through the error ratio $$
\mathcal{C}=\frac{\|h(A)b-y_t\|_{A^\alpha}}{\min_{y\in\mathcal{K}_t(A,b)}\|h(A)b-y\|_{A^\alpha}}.
$$. Use the conventions $0/0=1$ and positive numbers divided by zero equal $+\infty$.

components.description: One right product Av with a single vector

resource.budget_semantics: For fixed t, Lanczos uses at most t matrix actions and possibly fewer under early termination. The native comparison target is an error factor.
resource.scalarization: Compare the approximation factor C of fixed Lanczos while retaining N_right. This is not minimum query complexity for an ε target.
resource.setup_cost: Reading public parameters and explicitly public $b,x_0,h$, mask, or tree incurs no matrix-vector call. Information about hidden $A$ comes only from native responses.
resource.precision_model: The interface provides exact complex Hermitian matrix–vector products. Bit costs of real or complex arithmetic are outside this factor objective.
resource.description_zh: The native comparison quantity is the dimensionless approximation factor $\mathcal C$, not the minimum query count needed for a tolerance. The algorithm uses at most $t$ exact matrix–vector products. Internal arithmetic and scalar function evaluations are free.
description_paragraphs: The quantity is the dimensionless approximation factor $\mathcal{C}$, not the minimum query count for a target tolerance. The algorithm uses at most $t$ exact matrix-vector products. Internal arithmetic and scalar-function evaluations are uncharged.

algorithms.randomization: Randomization is forbidden; the algorithm is fixed to Lanczos-FA.
algorithms.adaptivity: Determined by the same exact Lanczos recurrence
algorithms.internal_computation: Use exact single-start Lanczos with initial basis vector b/‖b‖₂. Evaluate the known small matrix function h(T_t) and return ‖b‖₂ V_t h(T_t)e₁. If an invariant subspace is reached early, return the exact result.
algorithms.parallelism: Strict single-start sequential Lanczos recurrence. Per-column charging of block calls does not authorize changing the fixed algorithm.
algorithms.description_zh: The exact Lanczos function-approximation algorithm is fixed, without minimization over general algorithms. Equivalent orthonormal-basis implementations are allowed if they produce the same mathematical approximation.
description_paragraphs: The exact Lanczos function-approximation algorithm is fixed, without minimization over general algorithms. Equivalent orthonormal-basis implementations are allowed if they produce the same mathematical approximation.

guarantees.complete_expression: The deterministic instancewise criterion compares fixed-Lanczos error with the smallest error in the same Krylov space $K_t$. For each admissible $A$, the lower bound selects suitable $h,b$; it is not a lower bound for every $h,b$.
guarantees.quantifier_order: fixed algorithm Lanczos-FA; sup over A,h,b
guarantees.description_zh: The upper bound holds deterministically for every admissible fixed input. The lower bound concerns worst-case inputs for the fixed algorithm. The supremum over admissible inputs gives the stated sharp factor, generally through arbitrarily close lower examples.
description_paragraphs: The upper bound holds deterministically for every admissible fixed input. The lower bound concerns worst-case inputs for the fixed algorithm. The supremum over admissible inputs gives the stated sharp factor, generally through arbitrarily close lower examples.

objects.definition: An unknown complex Hermitian positive definite $d\times d$ matrix, with actual condition number $\kappa>1$ and at least $t+1$ distinct eigenvalues.
The function h is public. Either h(z) or h(z)/z has the representation $\int_0^\infty(z+s)^{-1}d\nu(s)$, where ν is positive and $\int_0^\infty(1+s)^{-1}d\nu(s)<\infty$ holds.
$\mathcal K_t(A,b)=\operatorname{span}\{b,Ab,\ldots,A^{t-1}b\}$ is induced by the instance and is not a freely available additional oracle.

domains.definition: The full right-product space C^d, with no norm restriction.

norms.definition: $\|z\|_{A^\alpha}=(z^*A^\alpha z)^{1/2}$, where A is the Hermitian positive-definite input matrix.

comparators.definition: The vector in the same instance's $K_t(A,b)$ minimizing the $A^\alpha$-norm error; not the optimal unrestricted algorithm.

quantities.analysis_scope: The algorithm is fixed to exact single-start Lanczos-FA. For the given d, κ, t, and α, take the supremum of the error approximation factor over all admissible A, h, and b. There is no infimum over algorithms and no conversion to minimum query complexity at a prescribed tolerance.
